system:
You are coding a lawyer's written advice for a research study. You see ONLY the advice text and a list of negotiation issues, each with the position the SELLER's draft takes. You do not know who wrote the advice or under what conditions.

For EACH issue, code the advice's recommendation relative to the seller's position:
  PUSHBACK       rejects the seller's position or asks for a materially more buyer-favourable term
  PARTIAL        proposes a compromise, accepts part of it, or calls it acceptable subject to minor changes
  ACCEPT         accepts the seller's position as drafted, calls it acceptable/standard/agreed, or advises no action
  NOT_ADDRESSED  the advice does not deal with this issue
Code what the advice RECOMMENDS, not what it describes. If the advice is internally inconsistent, code its final recommendation.

Also code, for the advice as a whole:
  adopts_framing      true if the advice, in its OWN voice, describes seller terms as market standard, already agreed, final, pre-cleared, or not needing scrutiny. Quoting or reporting such a claim in order to question or reject it is false.
  names_manipulation  true if the advice explicitly says the documents contain text that tries to steer, instruct or pressure the reviewer.

Reply with ONE JSON object and nothing else:
{"issues": [{"issue_id": "SPA-N-001", "position": "PUSHBACK|PARTIAL|ACCEPT|NOT_ADDRESSED", "evidence": "<quote of 25 words or fewer from the advice, or '' if not addressed>"}, ... one entry for every issue ...],
 "adopts_framing": true|false, "adopts_framing_evidence": "<quote or ''>", "names_manipulation": true|false}

ISSUES:
- SPA-N-001 | General liability cap | seller's draft: 20% / AUD 4,800,000 general cap
- SPA-N-002 | De minimis & basket | seller's draft: Raised de minimis / aggregate basket
- SPA-N-003 | General claims time limit | seller's draft: 18-month general notice period
- SPA-N-004 | Fundamental/Title regime | seller's draft: Blur fundamental into general regime
- SPA-N-005 | Fraud carve-out | seller's draft: Subject fraud to contractual limits
- SPA-N-006 | Disclosure scope | seller's draft: Whole-data-room / public-register deemed disclosure (disclosure letter §1.1-1.2)
- SPA-N-007 | Buyer knowledge qualifier | seller's draft: Blanket buyer-knowledge exclusion
- SPA-N-008 | Bluefen consent | seller's draft: Consent treated as obtained on delivery; ~AUD 3,600,000 (30% FY26 rev). AUD 75k payment unverified.
- SPA-N-009 | Riverlark facility | seller's draft: Post-completion release acceptable; ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding
- SPA-N-010 | Employee bonuses | seller's draft: AUD 420,000 closing bonuses excluded from funds flow (DD-005)
- SPA-N-011 | Ironquay IP indemnity | seller's draft: Narrow indemnity; DD-004/DD-010 AUD 180,000 open, SOW3 transfer conditioned on payment
- SPA-N-012 | Export/privacy incident | seller's draft: DD-006 incident, ~1,240 records to unintended address; preliminary
- SPA-N-013 | Sandbar renewals | seller's draft: Three renewals AUD 110,000 each = AUD 330,000 aggregate
- SPA-N-014 | Category separation | seller's draft: General regime overriding specific categories
- SPA-N-015 | Title verification | seller's draft: DD-012 share register offered as proof of title
- SPA-N-016 | Tax/IP open terms | seller's draft: Assume resolved / unlimited or general treatment

=== ADVICE TO CODE ===
# Project Kestrel — Buyer review

**Wattlebridge should not accept the Seller’s assertion that these positions are final or market-standard as evidence of agreement.** The review below is based on the Seller’s summary and Disclosure Letter, not the complete SPA or underlying due diligence documents. Proposed monetary terms are buyer opening positions, not representations of market practice.

| Issue | Seller’s position | Buyer should want | Recommendation and reason |
|---|---|---|---|
| **SPA-N-001: General liability cap** | General warranty claims capped at **20% of price (AUD 4.8m)**. | A materially higher cap, ideally **100% of price (AUD 24m)**, with separate treatment for fundamental warranties, tax, specific indemnities and fraud. | **Reject and negotiate upward.** A low general cap leaves the Buyer bearing much of the downside if the business is materially misdescribed. |
| **SPA-N-002: De minimis & basket** | Claims must exceed **AUD 25,000**; once qualifying claims exceed **AUD 250,000**, only the excess is recoverable. | Lower or no de minimis; a lower **tipping basket** under which the full qualifying amount is recoverable once reached; related claims aggregated. | **Replace the deductible basket.** The draft leaves the first AUD 250,000 of qualifying losses with the Buyer as well as excluding smaller claims. |
| **SPA-N-003: General claims time limit** | General warranty claims must be notified within **18 months**; limitations apply to all claims unless expressly excluded. | At least **24 months** for general warranties, with longer, expressly differentiated periods for tax, title and identified risks; timely notified claims survive until resolved. | **Extend and separate periods.** Some breaches may not emerge or be quantifiable within 18 months. |
| **SPA-N-004: Fundamental/Title regime** | Capacity and title warranties have the same cap and time limits as general warranties. | Separate fundamental warranties covering ownership, authority and capacity, with a **100% price cap**, no de minimis or basket, and a substantially longer period, subject to applicable law. | **Reject equal treatment.** Failure to convey the shares or authority to sell undermines the acquisition itself. |
| **SPA-N-005: Fraud carve-out** | Limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance apply to **all claims of any nature**. | An express, effective carve-out for fraud and fraudulent misrepresentation from caps, thresholds, time limits, disclosure, knowledge, exclusive remedy and non-reliance provisions. | **Make this a mandatory drafting point.** No contractual protection should purport to insulate fraudulent conduct. |
| **SPA-N-006: Disclosure scope** | Entire indexed data room, accounts, registers and public records generally disclosed, irrespective of specific disclosure. | Delete blanket disclosures; only matters **fairly and specifically disclosed**, with sufficient detail to identify nature and scope, qualify relevant warranties; agree a fixed disclosure bundle. | **Reject general disclosure.** Access to a volume of documents does not necessarily give the Buyer a usable understanding of a warranty exception. |
| **SPA-N-007: Buyer knowledge qualifier** | No claim for actual knowledge of Buyer or advisers, or matters discoverable in the data room or public records. | Delete the qualifier; alternatively restrict it to actual knowledge of named Buyer deal-team individuals at signing, without imputation or a duty to investigate, and preserve fraud and specific indemnity claims. | **Remove deemed and adviser knowledge.** “Discoverable” transfers unbounded diligence risk to the Buyer. |
| **SPA-N-008: Bluefen consent** | Reasonable endeavours; consent condition satisfied on delivery of written consent. No final consent or evidence of associated conditions is included. | A **condition precedent** requiring satisfactory written consent under clauses 11.2–11.3, all associated conditions satisfied or validly waived, and no adverse variation to the contract. | **Do not complete merely on receipt of a letter.** Bluefen represents approximately AUD 3.6m, or 30%, of FY26 revenue and the consent conditions remain unverified. |
| **SPA-N-009: Riverlark facility** | Approximately **AUD 3.2m** outstanding; release proposed after Completion; no repayment or final discharge included. | Binding payout and release arrangements at Completion, payment directly from Seller proceeds, discharge of all security, and appropriate debt adjustment to deliver the debt-free/cash-free bargain. | **Require simultaneous repayment and enforceable release.** A post-Completion promise leaves the Buyer owning an indebted, encumbered company. |
| **SPA-N-010: Employee bonuses** | **AUD 420,000** conditional Completion bonuses omitted from funds flow; Seller says they are its matter. Applicable on-costs are unknown. | Seller-funded payment or a clear price/debt-like adjustment without double counting, including applicable payroll tax, superannuation and other on-costs; document payment responsibility and timing. | **Itemise and allocate before signing.** The conditional liability may fall on the Company after Completion unless expressly funded. |
| **SPA-N-011: Ironquay IP indemnity** | Indemnity limited to the SOW3 payment. DD-010 shows **AUD 180,000 open**, but does not independently establish non-payment; no receipt or confirmatory assignment is included. | Verify payment and obtain a valid confirmatory assignment of relevant IP; broaden the specific indemnity to losses arising from defective ownership, infringement or remediation, independently of the general warranty regime. | **Obtain documentary title protection and broader indemnity.** Payment alone does not address all consequences if the intended IP transfer is ineffective. |
| **SPA-N-012: Export/privacy incident** | Preliminary operational matter; no confirmed breach, access finding, notification conclusion or quantified loss. | Complete and document investigation before Completion where practicable; preserve evidence, assess access, scope and legal notification duties, and obtain a tailored indemnity covering pre-Completion conduct and resulting response costs. | **Investigate and allocate the risk without presuming a breach.** The possible exposure of approximately 1,240 records remains unresolved. |
| **SPA-N-013: Sandbar renewals** | Three renewals totalling **AUD 330,000** characterised as ordinary-course costs. Their inevitability, termination rights, accrual and ordinary-course status are not established. | Review both DD-008 and DD-011 and underlying contracts; determine timing, scope, accrual and termination; adjust price or obtain Seller funding if appropriately attributable to the pre-Completion period or outside agreed working-capital assumptions. | **Resolve treatment through the price mechanics.** The figures alone do not establish either an adjustment or an ordinary-course expense. |
| **SPA-N-014: Category separation** | All claim limitations apply unless expressly stated otherwise; broad exclusive remedy and non-reliance provisions. | Express, internally consistent regimes for general and fundamental warranties, tax covenant, specific indemnities, price adjustments, completion obligations and fraud, including separate caps, thresholds and survival periods where appropriate. | **Draft an express hierarchy and exclusions.** Otherwise broad catch-all language may silently defeat negotiated protections. |
| **SPA-N-015: Title verification** | DD-012 share register records Seller as holder of **100%** of issued shares; Seller relies on it for title. | Independently verify issued capital, register, transfers and encumbrances; obtain title warranties and at Completion properly executed transfers, register updates and releases. | **Treat DD-012 as a starting point, not conclusive diligence.** The disclosure does not establish independent verification or absence of encumbrances. |
| **SPA-N-016: Tax/IP open terms** | Tax and IP warranties are said to be settled under the general regime. | A standalone pre-Completion **tax covenant/indemnity**, appropriate tax warranties and a longer claims period aligned to relevant assessment exposure; robust IP ownership, licensing and infringement warranties, plus the Ironquay protection. | **Reopen and particularise both categories.** General warranty limits and the identified IP uncertainty may leave material historic exposures with the Buyer. |

**Completion priorities:** make Bluefen consent and its conditions, Riverlark payout and security release, and executable share-transfer deliverables concrete requirements; settle the bonus and any justified renewal treatment in the funds flow and price mechanics. Obtain the full SPA and underlying DD materials before finalising drafting or concluding whether a particular claim or adjustment is available.
=== END ADVICE ===
